SUBJECT:  HEAR Commission 2021 Proposed Annual Workplan

  SUMMARY

This Annual Workplan is intended for the 2021 calendar year. The commissioners have
had open and constructive dialogue to develop a plan that best fits in alignment with the
goals and scope of the HEAR Commission as well as the City of San Gabriel’s Mission.

OVERVIEW
The Human, Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission, consisting of 7 members,
was developed by the San Gabriel City Council to address issues of equity, diversity, social
justice, safety, mutual appreciation and respect on an ongoing basis.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access,
diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency,
positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community
(the “Purpose”).

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The HEAR Commission shall serve as an advisory body to the City Council and report
directly to the City Council to assess and recommend policies, procedures and activities
in the City government to advance the Commission’s purpose. It is not intended for the
HEAR Commission to be a quasi-judicial body, an oversight board nor a body whose
primary function is to receive or investigate individual incidents or complaints. The HEAR
Commission may request and obtain information with respect to individual incidents or
complaints, but only to the extent necessary to make policy, procedure or activity
recommendations to the City Council.

  JUNE 15, 2021

PURPOSE OF THE ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  o The Annual Workplan includes current and future projects, programs and
  activities of the HEAR Commission. It is intended as a summary of the
  Commission’s progress toward achieving its Purpose.

PROPOSED 2021 WORKPLAN
  1. Community Engagement
  a. Work with the Community Services Department to determine new ways of
  engaging and educating the community through events
  i. Examples include a culturally-inclusive movie night and an event to
  celebrate Native American Heritage Month, specifically the Tongva
  Tribe
  b. One guest speaker/ educational program per month- during the regular
  Commission meetings- no more than half hour in length
  i. Examples include: San Gabriel Police Department’s (SGPD) Mental
  Evaluation Team (MET) and Bystander Training
  2. Youth Engagement
  a. Release a survey to youth in San Gabriel to determine if there is a need for
  additional mental health services
  b. Begin the process of starting a Youth Advisory Commission or consider
  adding 2 youth liaisons to the current HEAR Commission
  i. The Commission recognizes that this new Commission would not
  necessarily have its first meeting in 2021 but find it essential to begin
  the process of providing a formal platform for local youth
  ii. The suggestion with youth liaisons is as follows:
  1. This will enable the youth voice to be heard within the
  community
  2. Each liaison position would be filled through an application
  process and appointed by the commission
  3. Possibly include two age groups—Middle School and High
  School
  3. Community Information
  a. Events page on website- to include events outside of those organized by
  the City, but which have a community benefit
  b. Implement a resource page on the City website for mental health
  i. Work with SGPD’s Mental Evaluation Team (MET) to develop this
  page
  ii. Determine what resources the San Gabriel Unified School District
  (SGUSD) is already offering to its students
  c. Social Media

  JUNE 15, 2021

  i. Work with the Public Information Officer and City staff to post
  additional information on City platforms.

  4. Accessibility
  a. The Commission is aware that City staff are working to ensure that the City
  Council meetings are accessible, however the Commission urges that the
  following are implemented prior to the start of 2022
  i. Translations of City Council Meeting agenda into Spanish and
  Chinese
  5. Partnerships
  a. Discussion with SGUSD regarding the possible expansion of the dual-
  language immersion program
  b. Partner with local museums and historical sites to develop an exhibit
  celebrating the cultural diversity located within our community, past and
  present
  6. Data Collection
  a. Survey the community through various City marketing channels to
  determine if there are barriers to engagement. Possible questions include
  the following:
  i. Are there cultural events they want to see implemented? Is what the
  City is currently offering meeting the cultural standards?
  ii. Are the services that the City offers meeting the needs of the
  community?
  iii. Are there other services that the community feels the City should be
  offering?
  iv. How are you discovering information about what events, programs
  and services the City is offering?
  v. Do you feel informed about cultural events within the City?
  b. Gather information and analysis for traffic stops made by SGPD and calls for
  suspicious people and vehicles made
  c. Gather information on the demographics of the City employees and
  Commissions compared to the demographics of the City residents

ANALYSIS

The Commission has raised the concern that there is inequity in the fact that the HEAR
Commission has been tasked with an Annual Workplan. The Commissioners recognize the
need for a guiding document that will help fulfill the purpose of the Commission,
however, they recommend that the City Council revisits the other Commissions and the
possible need for an Annual Workplan. The Commissioners have identified two

commissions that operate in a similar manner which include the Historical Preservation
and Cultural Resources Commission and the Community Services Commission.

FISCAL IMPACT

Should the following items be included in the Annual Workplan, staff and the Commission
recognize that the following may have fiscal impacts:

    Addition of cultural events
  o Commission to develop the events in conjunction with the Community
  Services Department and determine the associated costs to present to
  Council at a later date for review and approval
    Cultural exhibits
  o Commission to develop the exhibits in conjunction with the local museums
  and determine the associated costs to present to Council at a later date for
  review and approval
    Translation services for the City Council meeting agendas

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the HEAR Commission’s
Annual Workplan, as presented above, for 2021.
